# glinet_wan (Resource)

Manages a wired WAN port of the router (`cable.set_config` in the router API). Use one instance of this resource for each wired WAN port.

~> **Warning:** a wrong configuration cuts the wired uplink of the router. Each write sends the full configuration of the protocol, as the web UI does: an attribute that is not set is removed on the router.

Only a router with a second wired WAN port (`software_feature.secondwan` of `system.get_info`) accepts `port = "secondwan"`: for that port, the provider reads `system.get_info` before each call and stops with an error when the router has no second wired WAN port. The reads of the second WAN port were not tested on a router, and what `cable.get_config` and `cable.set_config` do for the second WAN port on a router without one is not known. The role and the MAC address of the same port are in `glinet_wan_port`, which uses another router method; the two resources have only `port` in common. The write of this resource was not tested on a router; the parameters come from the router's web UI. Destroy removes the resource from the Terraform state and does not change the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "glinet_wan" "this" {
  protocol = "static"
  ipv4 = {
    ip      = "203.0.113.2"
    netmask = "255.255.255.0"
    gateway = "203.0.113.1"
    dns     = ["1.1.1.1", "8.8.8.8"]
  }
  mtu = 1500
}

# Only on a router with a second wired WAN port.
resource "glinet_wan" "second" {
  port     = "secondwan"
  protocol = "dhcp"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `protocol` (String) How the WAN port gets its address (`protocol` in the router API): `dhcp`, `static` or `pppoe`.

### Optional

- `ipv4` (Attributes) Static IPv4 configuration (`ipv4` in the router API). Required when `protocol` is `static`, and can be set only then. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ipv4))
- `ipv6` (Attributes) Static IPv6 configuration (`ipv6` in the router API). Can be set only when `protocol` is `static`. The web UI sends it only while IPv6 is enabled on the router (see `glinet_ipv6`). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ipv6))
- `mtu` (Number) MTU of the WAN port, 576 to 9200 (`mtu` in the router API). When it is not set, the provider does not send it. The web UI warns that IPv6 needs at least 1280.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) PPPoE password (`password` in the router API). Can be set only when `protocol` is `pppoe`. When it is not set, the provider sends an empty password, as the web UI does.
- `port` (String) The wired WAN port: `wan` for the first port or `secondwan` for the second port (`secondwan` in the router API). Default `wan`. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `ttl` (Number) IPv4 TTL that the router sets on the packets that it sends to the WAN, 1 to 255 (`ttl` in the router API). When it is not set, the provider does not send it.
- `ttl_ipv6` (Number) IPv6 hop limit that the router sets on the packets that it sends to the WAN, 1 to 255 (`ttl_ipv6` in the router API). When it is not set, the provider does not send it.
- `username` (String) PPPoE user name, at most 256 characters (`username` in the router API). Can be set only when `protocol` is `pppoe`. When it is not set, the provider sends an empty user name, as the web UI does.
- `vlan_id` (Number) VLAN ID of the WAN port, 1 to 4094 (`vlanid` in the router API). When it is not set, the provider does not send it.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `port`.

<a id="nestedatt--ipv4"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ipv4`

Required:

- `dns` (List of String) One or two IPv4 addresses of DNS servers (`dns` in the router API).
- `gateway` (String) IPv4 address of the gateway (`gateway` in the router API).
- `ip` (String) IPv4 address of the WAN port (`ip` in the router API).
- `netmask` (String) Netmask, for example `255.255.255.0` (`netmask` in the router API).


<a id="nestedatt--ipv6"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ipv6`

Required:

- `dns` (List of String) One or two IPv6 addresses of DNS servers (`dns` in the router API).
- `gateway` (String) IPv6 address of the gateway (`gateway` in the router API).
- `ip` (String) IPv6 address of the WAN port with a prefix length, for example `2001:db8::2/64` (`ip` in the router API).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is the port: "wan" or "secondwan".
terraform import glinet_wan.this wan
```
